raw_meta_yaml:
# Prioritize gpu build if cudatoolkit can be installed (through __cuda virtual package)
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "4.2.1"
  build_number: 5

  cuda: ${{ "enabled" if cuda_compiler_version != "None" else "disabled" }}
  cuda_build_string: cuda_${{ cuda_compiler_version | version_to_buildstring }}
  string_prefix: ${{ cuda_build_string if cuda ==  "enabled" else "cpu_" }}

recipe:
  name: colmap-split
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/colmap/colmap/archive/${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 15fb9e333541676e4ee9bc5d8ab95a3ed6e549a20eb13fc5aafd04ca06c76c88
    patches:
      - fix-onnx-include-path.patch
      # https://github.com/colmap/colmap/pull/4900
      - fix-msvc-lambda-odr.patch
      # pycolmap (python/CMakeLists.txt only)
      - bump-min-cmake.patch
      - if: win
        then: disable-parallel-builds.patch

build:
  number: ${{ build_number }}

outputs:
  - package:
      name: colmap
      version: ${{ version }}
    build:
      number: ${{ build_number }}
      string: ${{ string_prefix }}h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}
      variant:
        use_keys:
          # use cuda from the variant config, e.g. to build multiple CUDA variants
          - ${{ "cuda" if cuda == "enabled" }}
        # this will down-prioritize the cpu variant versus other variants of the package
        down_prioritize_variant: ${{ 0 if cuda == "enabled" else 1 }}
      script:
        file: build
        env:
          package_version: ${{ version }}

    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - if: cuda == "enabled"
          then: ${{ compiler('cuda') }}
        - cmake
        - if: unix
          then: make
        - pkg-config
        - ninja
        - if: osx
          then: llvm-openmp
        - if: linux
          then: libgomp
        - if: win
          then: m2-sed
      host:
        - if: unix
          then:
            - xorg-libxext
            - xorg-libxdmcp
            - xorg-libxau
            - libxcb
            - xorg-libxfixes
            - xorg-libxrender
            - xorg-libx11
            - xorg-libice
            - xorg-libsm
        - if: linux
          then:
            - libglu
            - libgl-devel
            - libopengl-devel
        - libblas
        - libcblas
        - libboost-devel
        - suitesparse
        - eigen
        - eigen-abi-devel
        - freeimage
        - glog
        - gflags
        - glew
        - cgal-cpp
        - ceres-solver
        - if: cuda == "enabled"
          then: ceres-solver * [build="gpu*"]
          else:
            - ceres-solver * [build="cpu*"]
            # avoid pulling the CUDA build of faiss (and with it CUDA) into cpu builds
            - faiss * [build="*_cpu"]
            - libfaiss * [build="*_cpu"]
        - qt6-main
        - git
        - flann
        - sqlite
        - if: unix
          then:
            - vlfeat
            - gmp
        - lz4-c
        - metis
        # libopenimageio (not the openimageio metapackage) so that its run_exports
        # (libopenimageio >=x.y.z,<x.(y+1)) apply; the metapackage has none, and the
        # libopenimageio pinning/migrations only see this name.
        - libopenimageio
        # OpenImageIOConfig.cmake does find_dependency(fmt) (header-only use)
        - fmt
        - poselib
        - faiss
        - libfaiss
        - if: cuda == "enabled"
          then:
            - libcurand-dev
            - cuda-cudart-dev
            - cuda-version ==${{ cuda_compiler_version }}
            - faiss-gpu
        - if: osx
          then: llvm-openmp
        - if: linux
          then: libgomp
        - if: not (osx and x86_64)
          then:
            - onnxruntime
            - onnxruntime-cpp
      run:
        - flann
        - if: cuda == "enabled"
          then:
            - __cuda >=${{ cuda_compiler_version }}  # needed to ensure cuda packages are only installed in cuda environments and fallback to cpu builds otherwise
        - if: unix
          then:
            - xorg-libxext
            - xorg-libxdmcp
            - xorg-libxau
            - libxcb
            - xorg-libxfixes
            - xorg-libxrender
            - xorg-libx11
            - xorg-libice
            - xorg-libsm
            - vlfeat
        - if: linux
          then: libglu
      ignore_run_exports:
        by_name:
          # only fmt::fmt-header-only via OpenImageIO, nothing is linked
          - fmt
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('colmap', upper_bound='x.x') }}

    tests:
      - script:
          - if: win
            then:
              - if exist %PREFIX%\\Library\\bin\\colmap.exe (exit 0) else (exit 1)
              - if exist %PREFIX%\\Library\\lib\\colmap_exe.lib (exit 0) else (exit 1)
              - if: cuda == "enabled"
                then: if exist %PREFIX%\\Library\\lib\\colmap_cuda.lib (exit 0) else (exit 1)
          - if: unix
            then:
              - test -f $PREFIX/bin/colmap
              - test -f $PREFIX/lib/libcolmap_exe.a
              - test -f $PREFIX/share/colmap/colmap-config.cmake
              - if: cuda == "enabled"
                then: test -f $PREFIX/lib/libcolmap_util_cuda.a

    about:
      license: BSD-3-Clause
      license_file:
        - COPYING.txt
        - src/thirdparty/LSD/LICENSE
        - src/thirdparty/PoissonRecon/LICENSE
        - src/thirdparty/SiftGPU/LICENSE
        - src/thirdparty/VLFeat/LICENSE
      summary: COLMAP is a general-purpose Structure-from-Motion (SfM) and Multi-View Stereo (MVS) pipeline with a graphical and command-line interface.
      homepage: https://colmap.github.io/


  - package:
      name: pycolmap
      version: ${{ version }}
    build:
      number: ${{ build_number }}
      string: ${{ string_prefix }}h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}
      variant:
        use_keys:
          # use cuda from the variant config, e.g. to build multiple CUDA variants
          - ${{ "cuda" if cuda == "enabled" }}
        # this will down-prioritize the cpu variant versus other variants of the package
        down_prioritize_variant: ${{ 0 if cuda == "enabled" else 1 }}
      script:
        - if: win
          then:
            - set CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
            - set CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=1
            - set CMAKE_ARGS=-G Ninja
            - set CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=1
            # Kill LTCG/IPO and PDBs to reduce linker memory
            - set CMAKE_ARGS=%CMAKE_ARGS% -DCMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION=OFF
            - set CMAKE_ARGS=%CMAKE_ARGS% -DCMAKE_MSVC_DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT=""
            - set CMAKE_ARGS=%CMAKE_ARGS% -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="/INCREMENTAL:NO /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF"
            - set CMAKE_ARGS=%CMAKE_ARGS% -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="/INCREMENTAL:NO /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF"
            - set "FAISS_CMAKE=%LIBRARY_PREFIX%\lib\cmake\faiss\faiss-targets.cmake"
            - sed -i "s|INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES \".*\"|INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES \"faiss\"|g" "%FAISS_CMAKE%"
            - set CUDAFLAGS=--use-local-env
        - if: osx
          then: CXXFLAGS="${CXXFLAGS} -D_LIBCPP_DISABLE_AVAILABILITY"
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then: export CMAKE_ARGS="${CMAKE_ARGS} -DGENERATE_STUBS=OFF"
        - ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-build-isolation --no-deps

    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - if: cuda == "enabled"
          then: ${{ compiler('cuda') }}
        - cmake
        - if: unix
          then: make
        - ninja
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
            - pybind11
            - pybind11-stubgen
            - numpy
            - scikit-build
            - scikit-build-core
        - if: osx
          then: llvm-openmp
        - if: linux
          then: libgomp
        - if: win
          then: m2-sed
      host:
        - if: linux
          then: libgl-devel
        - pip
        - python
        - scikit-build
        - scikit-build-core
        - pybind11
        # run_exports `pybind11-abi ==<internals version>`: pycolmap passes
        # ceres::Problem / CostFunction objects to pyceres, which only works if both
        # were built with the same pybind11 internals version.
        - pybind11-abi
        - pybind11-stubgen
        - numpy
        - ruff
        - black
        - isort
        - libboost-devel
        # the colmap output built from the same source in this job
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('colmap', exact=True) }}
        - if: cuda == "disabled"
          then:
            # avoid pulling CUDA builds (and with them CUDA) into cpu builds
            - ceres-solver * [build="cpu*"]
            - libfaiss * [build="*_cpu"]
        - eigen-abi-devel
        - libblas
        - libcblas
        - cgal-cpp
        - sqlite
        - flann
        - glog
        - gflags
        - flann
        - freeimage
        - metis
        - ceres-solver
        - glew
        - if: unix
          then: vlfeat
        - gmp
        - qt6-main
        - lz4-c
        - fmt
        - libfaiss
        # libopenimageio (not the openimageio metapackage): only it carries
        # run_exports (libopenimageio >=x.y.z,<x.(y+1)), and only this name is
        # tracked by the global pinning / migrator.
        - libopenimageio
        - if: cuda == "enabled"
          then:
            - cuda-cudart-dev ${{ cuda_compiler_version }}.*
            - libcurand-dev
            - cuda-version ${{ cuda_compiler_version }}.*
      run:
        - python
        - numpy
        - if: cuda == "enabled"
          then: __cuda >=${{ cuda_compiler_version }}

    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - pycolmap
          pip_check: false
      - requirements:
          run:
            - pip
        script:
          - pip check
          - python -c "import pycolmap; reconstruction = pycolmap.Reconstruction(); x = reconstruction.points3D"

    about:
      license: BSD-3-Clause
      license_file:
        - COPYING.txt
      summary: pycolmap exposes to Python most COLMAP reconstruction objects, such as Cameras and Points3D, as well as estimators for absolute and relative poses.
      homepage: https://colmap.github.io/


about:
  license: BSD-3-Clause
  license_file:
    - COPYING.txt
    - src/thirdparty/LSD/LICENSE
    - src/thirdparty/PoissonRecon/LICENSE
    - src/thirdparty/SiftGPU/LICENSE
    - src/thirdparty/VLFeat/LICENSE
  summary: COLMAP is a general-purpose Structure-from-Motion (SfM) and Multi-View Stereo (MVS) pipeline with a graphical and command-line interface.
  homepage: https://colmap.github.io/

extra:
  feedstock-name: colmap
  recipe-maintainers:
    - Tobias-Fischer
